root_cause.text: In `fs/iomap/buffered-io.c`’s `iomap_read_folio_iter()`, `ctx->cur_folio` was only cleared when the full folio was submitted, so in the `!ifs` case with smaller I/O granularity than `folio_size()` the folio remained referenced and `iomap_read_end()` later accessed a folio already owned by the I/O helper.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the handoff condition from `if (*bytes_submitted == folio_len)` to `if (*bytes_submitted == folio_len || !ifs)` and the commit message explains that when `1 << inode->i_blkbits` matches folio size but I/O is done in smaller chunks, “`iomap_read_end()` will still be called on the folio even though the IO helper owns it,” causing invalid folio access.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a local iomap folio state pointer in preparation for folio-state handling within iomap_read_folio_iter().
intent_record.what: A new local variable declaration, `struct iomap_folio_state *ifs;`, was added to `iomap_read_folio_iter()` alongside the existing local variables.
intent_record.how: This change only introduces a pointer variable into the function scope; by itself, it does not alter control flow or runtime behavior in the shown hunk, but it prepares the function to access folio state information later in the function body.

intent_record.intent_summary: Capture the result of `ifs_alloc()` so the folio read path retains the allocated state instead of ignoring it.
intent_record.what: The call `ifs_alloc(iter->inode, folio, iter->flags);` was changed to an assignment: `ifs = ifs_alloc(iter->inode, folio, iter->flags);`.
intent_record.how: This stores the return value of `ifs_alloc()` in the local variable `ifs` instead of discarding it, allowing subsequent code to use that allocated context/state during folio read handling. It likely fixes a missing use of the allocator's result.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix folio ownership handoff so the IO helper can complete reads even when no `ifs` is attached to the folio.
intent_record.what: The comment above the folio handoff condition was expanded to describe two cases for transferring folio ownership to the IO helper, and the condition was changed from `*bytes_submitted == folio_len` to `*bytes_submitted == folio_len || !ifs`, so `ctx->cur_folio` is also cleared when there is no `ifs` attached.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code now hands ownership of the current folio to the IO helper not only when the whole folio has been submitted, but also when the folio has no associated `ifs` structure. This allows the IO helper to complete and end the read for folios even when the filesystem or block device uses a smaller IO granularity than the folio size, preventing the caller from retaining ownership incorrectly.

The group directly matches the root cause: it fixes folio ownership handoff in the buffered I/O read path, specifically for the !ifs case where the folio was not cleared after partial submission and could later be accessed incorrectly by iomap_read_end().

candidates.rationale: This condition only clears ctx->cur_folio when the entire folio has been submitted. In the buggy !ifs path with smaller I/O granularity than folio_size(), the folio could remain referenced after partial submission, leading iomap_read_end() to later operate on a folio already handed off to the I/O helper.

This statement tracks how much of the folio has been submitted, and the subsequent ownership handoff depends on it. The vulnerability arises because the folio is only released based on full submission, so partial progress leaves ctx->cur_folio pointing at a folio that the I/O helper may already own.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition gated clearing ctx->cur_folio on full folio submission only. In the vulnerable !ifs case with smaller I/O granularity than folio_size(), partial submission left the folio referenced, so iomap_read_end() could later access a folio already handed off to the I/O helper.

This statement advances the submitted-byte count that the ownership handoff logic depends on. Because the folio was only released when the full folio was submitted, partial progress here contributed to ctx->cur_folio remaining set after the folio had been partially handed to the I/O helper.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet shows the fix for the reported invalid folio access. In `iomap_read_folio_iter()`, after submitting read bytes, it now clears `ctx->cur_folio` when the whole folio was read: `if (*bytes_submitted == folio_len) ctx->cur_folio = NULL;`. This prevents later access after the IO helper has taken ownership. The end path was also changed to only call `iomap_read_end()` when `ctx->cur_folio` is still set: `if (ctx->cur_folio) iomap_read_end(ctx->cur_folio, bytes_submitted);`. Additionally, for the `!ifs` case, `iomap_read_end()` now warns if bytes were submitted and only unlocks the folio when `!bytes_submitted`, matching the new ownership rules. Therefore the vulnerable construct is not present in this commit version, and the fix is already included.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present in this version. In the old buggy behavior, `ctx->cur_folio`/folio ownership was not cleared when only part of a folio was submitted, causing later `iomap_read_end()` to act on a folio already owned by the I/O helper. This diff changes the read accounting and end handling so that ownership is tracked correctly: `iomap_read_end()` now explicitly handles the case where `ifs->read_bytes_pending` is already zero and only unlocks when `!bytes_submitted` and there is no `ifs`, while the iter path now increments `*bytes_submitted` only after `read_folio_range()` succeeds (`ret = ctx->ops->read_folio_range(...); if (ret) return ret; *bytes_submitted += plen;`). The added `WARN_ON_ONCE(ifs->read_bytes_pending != 0); ifs->read_bytes_pending = len + 1;` also prevents accumulation from prior state. These changes indicate the fix is already present, and the specific buggy construct from the root cause is not shown here.
